about: The first blind ratings of doc 84's Slice 2 packet (artifacts/talk/rate/s2/packet.md, 90 conversations), by three raters given only the packet, never key.json: each item rated 1-5 for how believable it is as real people talking and how coherent (each line follows the one before), with a note on the low ones. The raters' own words and numbers, unchanged; scored by tools/talk_rate.py score (h1.json, h1.md).

ratings.note: 'Good plan' to a wistful wish, then 'It stank' about nothing named. The lines don't connect.
The child asks a direct question and gets a bare 'Well!', which doesn't answer it.
A greeting is stapled to an unexplained line about the Kestrel. The reply only loosely fits and the talk ends at once.
'When it hits my supper' is a food-price retort, but the news is about planks.
'Close?' gets 'One of many', and 'Sleep sound' gets 'Much'. Neither answers the line before it.
Word salad. The well gets a tavern-floor reply, there's a knock-knock punchline with no setup, a speaker talks twice with unrelated lines, and nobody answers anybody.
They say farewell mid-talk and then carry on. Replies like 'something else next week' and 'That's done, then' don't follow, and the cells news gets 'It'll mend'.
Hanne offers to 'just listen' to a remark, Aud leaves, and a third speaker who wasn't in the talk says goodbye. The opener repeats 'back'.
The child asks 'Is that bad?' and gets 'Is that so.' The question goes unanswered.
Sybil says 'I'll see you' mid-talk. Soren goes on, and the warning about a local stranger gets 'News from far off'.
The news is about berries and the reply is about glass. The opener's 'talking wagons lately, too' is clumsy.
'I'll let you be' gets 'Of course you have', which answers nothing.
'Rolling in something' is an odd answer to soft water. A goodbye comes in the middle, then Karin names her home though nobody asked.
'Is that so. Thank you for telling me.' is stiff, formal filler, not neighbourly talk.
The sausage daydream gets a curt 'Good day to you, then'. It's ignored, and the talk just ends.
Ulla says goodbye straight after robbery news, then Dorcas carries on anyway.
'Don't stay up late' doesn't follow a memory, and 'you'd not believe me if I told you' answers nothing.
'Bless everyone' gets 'I dozed. Don't tell.' The two lines have nothing to do with each other.
'Night, then' in the morning, mid-talk. 'Not the eels' answers a question nobody asked, and the thread falls apart.
Nonsense: pie, the chapel, 'They were wrong', 'He looked bald'. No line answers another.
A calving cow gets a reply about fishing, then a goodbye.
The tax grumble gets 'Off to bed with you' and 'All the better', then a third speaker barges in.
'Back so soon?' is stapled to a heavy confession. It gets a bare 'Aye' and an immediate goodbye.
The apprentice's dropped tray gets only 'Take care, now'. It doesn't engage.
'Think nothing of it' answers a thanks that was never given, and 'Them too' means nothing.
A string of stock farewells and non-answers ('Who would I tell?', 'And then what?') after the theft news. No exchange holds together.
Clumsy stacked opener. 'Nobody's blaming you' doesn't follow Ansel's line, then an abrupt bedtime exit.
A race to the well gets 'A mouse, or a rat?', a complete non sequitur.
'Longest day of my life' gets 'Maybe! Who?' and then 'Well, well'. Nonsense.
'I'll call on' the accused thief gets 'You're right. We shouldn't.' The reply contradicts the line it answers.
Repeated 'Bless you, shore-friend', gibberish ('Rain coast, rain salt, no salt'), and topic jumps with no replies.
Three stacked openers, then Oda answers the theft news with 'Go well' and 'Off home, then'. She ignores it.
'We managed' answers good news as if it were hardship. Then an abrupt brush-off.
Firewood news gets 'And you. Sleep easy.', answering a farewell nobody gave, and the same line is repeated word for word.
Wagon price news is answered with 'And you. Sleep easy.', a farewell to something nobody said, and then the same line again word for word.
'In my day it was the same, and we managed' answers plenty as if it were hardship, and the talk then drops into stock goodbyes. Opening a meat-tonight remark with 'You again?' is also stilted.
The opener piles three stock gossip lead-ins on top of each other. The listener replies 'Go well' to the news, and nobody really answers anybody.
Word salad: 'Bless you, shore-friend' twice in reply to nothing, 'Rain coast, rain salt, no salt', 'It feels like the cheap cloth'. No line answers the one before.
Saying you'll call on the accused thief to see how they are is odd. 'You're right. We shouldn't.' agrees with something that was never said.
'Good old Grayrock' comes out of nowhere, since the wagon's origin was never named, and 'Fair weights, friend' answers neither line.
'Longest day of my life' gets 'Maybe! Who?', then 'Well, well.' Pure non sequiturs.
A bet to race to the well is answered with 'A mouse, or a rat?', which has nothing to do with it.
The opener is overstuffed with stock fragments ('Twice in a day', 'We'd only just finished'). 'Nobody's blaming you' doesn't follow from the weather remark, and the talk ends abruptly.
Theft gossip is met with 'And you. Mind the dark.', then 'Who would I tell?' and 'And then what?' answer nothing. It is a string of goodbyes and warnings with no exchange.
Praise for someone's apprenticeship gets 'Think nothing of it', as if thanked, then 'Ha. Them too.', which is meaningless.
A small complaint (the dropped tray) is met with 'Take care, now'. The listener ignores it entirely.
The greeting swerves into an unprompted lament about losing a house, and it gets a bare 'Aye' and an immediate goodbye.
A tax grumble gets 'Off to bed with you', then 'All the better', then a third speaker barges in. Nothing connects.
The opening sentence ('We'd only just finished with the last of this') is confusing, and 'Keep your purse close' is a generic tag that doesn't fit a smokehouse break-in.
Calving news is answered with a remark about fishing, then a goodbye. A complete non sequitur.
Nonsense chain: 'Don't say pie', 'Whatever the chapel's giving', 'They were wrong', 'He looked bald'. No thread at all.
'Night, then' cuts in mid-topic, and 'Not the eels. The quiet.' answers a question nobody asked.
'Bless you. Bless everyone.' as a greeting is strange, and 'I dozed. Don't tell.' bears no relation to it.
If she can't empty the full cash box, the cutpurse gets everything, so 'Then the cutpurse gets nothing' contradicts the line before it.
'Don't stay up late' doesn't answer a memory, 'Fields and a ford' hangs alone, and 'you'd not believe me' comes from the wrong speaker.
'Right. Till next time.' brushes off the robbery news, and the speaker then carries on as though no goodbye had been said.
A playful wish about sausages is met with a flat goodbye. No engagement at all.
'Is that so. Thank you for telling me.' is stiff and formal, like a clerk rather than a neighbour hearing of a wedding.
'Have you tried rolling in something?' doesn't answer the water complaint. 'Coldwater, where the High Road starts to climb' answers an unasked question after a goodbye.
Theft news gets 'I'll let you be', then 'Of course you have', which answers nothing.
The news is that berries are dear, and the reply talks about glass on the roads. Mismatched.
'I'll see you' comes as a goodbye mid-topic. 'News from far off' answers a warning about a local stranger.
The child asks 'Is that bad?', and the adult's 'Is that so.' ignores the question.
A good opening line, but the talk immediately becomes an onlooker's line and goodbyes, and a fourth person who never spoke says the farewell.

Disjointed fragments: 'Farewell' comes mid-conversation and then the talk carries on, a speech about the roads answers nothing, and the stock fillers ('So it goes', 'It'll mend') don't respond to anything.
Total word salad: well, tavern floor, a goose joke, 'Did so', 'A maybe's a yes with its boots off'. No line follows from the one before.
'Close?' gets 'One of many', and 'Sleep sound.' gets 'Much.' After the first line, nothing fits.
Planks being dear wouldn't 'hit my supper'. The stock reply about prices doesn't fit the goods.
The opener jumps from a greeting to an unexplained ship ('the Kestrel'). The reply is only loosely related, and the talk goes straight to goodbyes.
The child asks 'Is that bad?' and gets only 'Well!', which doesn't answer it. The exchange stops dead.
Wanting to ride the carts gets 'Good plan', then 'It stank' refers to nothing, and the advice to pray doesn't fit any of it.
'It stank' has nothing to refer back to after the line about the cart. 'Good plan' and 'say a prayer' are stock replies that don't engage with what Gwen said.
The child asks a direct question and the bare 'Well!' never answers it.
The reply about the price hitting 'my supper' doesn't fit planks, which aren't food. The opener's 'Frosthollow... Frosthollow wagon' is clumsy.
'One of many' doesn't answer 'Close?', and 'Sleep sound.' / 'Much.' is gibberish as an exchange.
A string of unrelated lines: the well, then a tavern floor, then a goose joke, then 'Did so'. One speaker talks twice in a row and nobody answers anybody.
Maren says farewell halfway through and then keeps talking. The lines are non sequiturs about roads and the cells, and the stock closers ('It'll mend') fit nothing that came before.
The opener is garbled ('Back again? Back home...'). Hanne's 'I'll just listen' answers nothing, and a third speaker says goodbye out of nowhere.
'I'll let you be' brushes the gossip off, and 'Of course you have' doesn't follow from it at all.
'Rolling in something' is a strange answer to water that tastes wrong. Goodbyes come in the middle, and the line about Coldwater's fishing folk answers nothing.

'I dozed. Don't tell.' has no link to 'Bless you. Bless everyone.'
Nonsense: pie, then the chapel, then 'They were wrong', then 'He looked bald'. No line connects to the one before it.
A cow calving gets a reply about fishing. Total non sequitur.
'Off to bed with you' answers the tax complaint with nothing, 'All the better' doesn't follow, and a third speaker barges in at the end.
The apprentice story gets only a farewell, a non-response nobody would give to that.
'Think nothing of it' answers praise for a third party as if it were thanks, and 'Ha. Them too.' is meaningless.
The opener stacks three unrelated openers. 'Nobody's blaming you' doesn't follow Ansel's remark, and the exchange then just stops.
'Maybe! Who?' has no connection to 'the longest day of my life', and 'Well, well' closes nothing.

Word salad: 'Bless you, shore-friend' is said twice to unrelated lines, 'Rain coast, rain salt, no salt' means nothing, and the reply about cheap cloth answers a line about a stranger nursing a drink.
The opener piles three openers onto the news. Oda answers the theft with 'Go well' and 'Off home', ignoring it completely.
'We managed' implies hardship, which makes no sense as a reply to news that meat will be plentiful. Then the talk just ends.
The Kestrel comes up with no context, the reply about 'a thousand' only loosely connects, and the pair go straight to goodbyes.
The child's question 'Is that bad?' gets 'Is that so.', which neither answers it nor fits.
Sybil says goodbye, then Soren carries on with a warning, and Sybil answers it with 'News from far off', which doesn't fit a stranger close by.
Berries are dear, and the reply is about glass. A mismatched reply.
The sausage daydream gets only a farewell. Nobody answers anybody.
Ulla says goodbye to robbery news, then Dorcas carries on as if she hadn't.
'Don't stay up late' doesn't answer a memory coming back, 'Fields and a ford' hangs in the air, and Corwin's last line answers nothing.
The logic falls apart. If there's nowhere to empty the cash box, it stays full, so 'Then the cutpurse gets nothing' is backwards. 'Like a drum' is unclear too.
'Morning' turns into 'Night, then' halfway through, 'Not the eels' refers to nothing, and the replies don't line up.
The opening sentence ('finished with the last of this') makes no sense, and 'Keep your purse close' doesn't fit a raid on the smokehouse.
A personal confession about losing a house gets 'Aye' and an immediate goodbye. The opener's greeting is spliced awkwardly onto it.
Farewells are scattered through it, 'Who would I tell?' and 'And then what?' answer nothing, and the theft news is never taken up.
'A mouse, or a rat?' has nothing to do with a race to the well.
'Good old Grayrock' comes from nowhere (wagon day, but no place was named), and 'Fair weights, friend' doesn't follow.
'You're right. We shouldn't.' doesn't follow Imogen's plan to call on Rosamund, and it's odd to call on the accused thief rather than the victim.
The news about firewood prices gets 'And you. Sleep easy.', and that same line is repeated word for word at the end.
